newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto Sun shareholders approve buyout.
newsitem.headline: Toronto Sun shareholders approve buyout.

text.p: Toronto Sun Publishing Corp said on Tuesday that shareholders at a special meeting approved a management group's C$16 a share bid for the newspaper company.
Chairman Lionel Schipper told shareholders the deal would close on October 7 if the plan of arrangement allowing management to take the company private won court approval on Wednesday.
The buyout would return Toronto Sun to its roots as a tightly held company with lots of employee involvement, Schipper said.

The company will have a nine-member board, on which two members will be memed by CIBC Wood Gundy, two will be independents and two will be management appointees. The Ontario Teachers Pension Plan will appoint three members.

Schipper admitted the next quarter-century may be tough. But he added that the first 25 years were hard for the Sun, which grew out of the defunct Toronto Telegram in the early 1970s, and it successfully weathered that storm.

"In any new company, there are always tough decisions... when you have C$250 million of debt, you have to look at things a little differently than when you are debt-free," management team leader Paul Godfrey told reporters after the meeting.
"We will be looking at every possibility of how we handle that C$250 million in debt," he added.
Godfrey did not rule out either asset sales or staff cuts. Many analysts believe Toronto Sun's debt may force it to sell its 60.2 percent holding in the Financial Post newspaper.

Reports last week said Conrad Black's Southam Inc was interested in Toronto Sun's holding in the daily business tabloid. But chief financial officer Bruce Jackson on Monday said the management group had not received any bids for the asset and were interested in keeping it.
"I would consider every possibility...Everything is on the table but I am not going to get specific because that is unfair," he told reporters.
"We have not made any decisions yet," Godfrey said.
He indicated that current plans are to keep the Sun group intact, despite the onerous debtload.
"We made a bid for all the assets of the Sun group and if we had any other intentions, we would have to reveal them in the information circular," Godfrey said.
Godfrey was unable to confirm whether Schipper will stay on as chairman of the company. He said this is something which the team is still discussing.
The management team emerged victorious in an auction Rogers Communications Inc held earlier this summer for its 63 percent holding in the company.

Although speculation that Quebecor Inc could step in with an eleventh-hour bid appears to have little foundation given the smooth progress of the management takeover through shareholder approval, Schipper admitted that another party has the right to make a higher offer up until the closing on October 7.
-- Sarah Edmonds, Reuters Toronto Bureau (416) 941-8100, E-mail sarah.edmonds@reuters.com
